records.name: East Passyunk Crossing Civic Association (EPX)
records.summary: Neighbors in the East Passyunk area who follow zoning and development plans and meet monthly to talk them over. The group also runs volunteer cleanups, tree care and a community garden, and hosts neighborhood events such as a fall festival.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans and attend a monthly membership meeting. Volunteers can help with cleanups, tree care and the community garden, and the group hosts neighborhood events like Fall Fest.

schedule.text: General membership meetings on the first Monday of each month at 7 pm, online on Zoom for now.

access.notes: Monthly meetings are online on Zoom for now, according to the group's site.

first_step.how: Sign up for the group's mailing list to get the monthly Zoom details, then join the first Monday meeting at 7 pm.
first_step.basis: The site gives a fixed monthly meeting time, an online way in and a mailing list sign-up. It does not say whether non-members may speak or vote.
first_step.what_to_expect: Monthly general membership meetings run online on Zoom, and the October 2026 calendar lists the next one from 7 to 8:30 pm. The site does not say who usually attends or what the agenda covers, and it does not mention dues.
first_visit_tips: Get on the mailing list early so the Zoom details reach you before the meeting.
The group also holds separate zoning meetings, so check the events page for the next one if zoning is your interest.
Log in a few minutes early to test your audio and video.

records.notes: The events page lists five October 2026 items: membership meeting on Oct 5, zoning meeting on Oct 12, board meeting on Oct 19, a happy hour on Oct 20 and Fall Fest on Oct 31, so status is active. The newest news post is dated Sept 23, 2025. The Monthly Meetings page says Zoom details appear in the newsletter or on the Community News page, but the news page shows no current link. The site's general contact address is contact@epcrossing.org; the tier 1 zoning address is kept. Event listings do not say who can attend. The community garden page describes 44 individual plots on the Ss. Neumann-Goretti campus, a waitlist form, and 8 plots set aside for immigrants and refugees; the garden may deserve its own record. Meetings occasionally move to Bok, weather permitting. No SEPTA stop is named on the site, so none is added.

records.name: East Point Breeze Neighbors
records.summary: A City-registered neighborhood group for the Point Breeze area. Neighbors join committees on zoning, outreach, technology, cleanups and public safety, and the group holds general meetings and community events.
records.what_you_do: Members join committees such as Planning and Zoning and Clean & Green, attend general meetings and community events, and help elect the board, which members in good standing choose.

locations.label: Contact address (City list)
locations.address: PO Box 54891, Philadelphia, PA 19148, Philadelphia, PA 19146

first_step.how: Text the keyword epbn to 77948 or join the monthly email newsletter to get meeting and event notices, then come to a general meeting.
first_step.basis: The site invites area residents and property owners to general meetings and offers reminder sign-ups, but it gives no meeting dates or place, so the first way in is not clear until you sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not give meeting dates, times, places or a Zoom link, and it does not say whether people who do not live or own property in the area may attend. It lists five committees you can join: Planning and Zoning, Community Outreach, Technology, Clean & Green and Public Safety. The site mentions no dues or fees.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the next general meeting date through the contact page before you go, since the site lists none.
Ask a committee chair, listed on the contact page, how and when that committee meets.
If zoning is your interest, read the group's Zoning and Planning Information page first, as the site asks.

records.notes: No dated meeting, event or news item was found on the site. The newest dated items are a 2023 tax filing (no month shown) and a December 2019 constitution, and the events page returned HTTP 404. Because nothing dated falls within the last 12 months, status is probably_active rather than active. last_sign_of_life and its URL are still the City registry entry, so the reviewer may want to confirm or downgrade. A web search found only a 2016 article about the group's name change and no 2026 meeting notice. Meeting place Zoom and the PO Box address come from the City list, not the site.

records.name: Fitler Square Neighborhood Association
records.summary: Fitler Square Neighborhood Association is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the South part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Markward Playground, 400 S. Taney Street, Philadelphia, PA 19146

first_step.how: Email the contact listed for the association, or write to its PO Box 3918, to ask when it next meets, since the site lists no meetings.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says no dues are needed to get the group's advocacy and information, and a Join link exists, but the join page could not be read (HTTP 403) and no meetings or events are listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit, and its events page lists no upcoming events. The news archive covers posts from 2019 to 2023 on traffic, bike lanes and neighborhood history, so ask first whether a meeting is planned. The FAQ says no dues are needed to take part in its advocacy, information and support.
first_visit_tips: Check the news page for recent posts before you contact the group.
Ask whether non-members can attend meetings, since the site does not say.
Ask about the next opportunity to give input on a local project.

records.notes: Status changed to dormant. The newest dated item on the news page is March 31, 2023, which is more than 24 months old, and the events page says there are no events yet. The City registry date (2026-10) was not treated as a dated post. The Join page returned HTTP 403, so it was not read; it is the likely route in, and the reviewer may want to confirm how to join. The About page says the group was formed in 2018 and that homeowners, condo residents, renters and businesses should all be represented. The news page names South of South Neighborhood Association as the group behind a 2023 gateway project (lead, not checked). Facebook and Twitter/X pages are linked in the footer and were not used. Reviewer should decide whether a dormant group stays public.

records.name: Girard Estate Area Residents (GEAR)
records.summary: Girard Estate Area Residents (GEAR) is one of the community organizations registered with the City to review nearby zoning and building proposals in the South part of the city. Neighbors can follow what is planned and speak up.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: Donatucci Library, 20th & Shunk St, Phila PA 19145

first_step.how: Use the contact form or the email address on the group's website to ask about the next meeting, since the site lists no meeting times.
first_step.basis: The website is marked as a new site in development. It lists no meetings, events or join steps beyond a contact form, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The website does not describe a first visit, meeting times or who attends, and it lists no events or dates. Expect to contact the group first to learn when and where it meets. The site does not mention dues or fees.

records.notes: The site is marked as a new website in development. Its About, Events and Contact pages returned HTTP 404. The site's only date is a 2026 copyright footer, which is not evidence, so status is probably_active and the City registry date is kept. The website at this address calls itself Girard Estate Neighbors Association, the separate record below that shares this address. The reviewer should check whether GEAR and GENA are one group before both are published. Meeting place is from the City list and is not confirmed by the site.

records.name: Girard Estate Neighbors Association
records.summary: A neighborhood group the City of Philadelphia has registered to be consulted on zoning and development in the South part of the city, Girard Estate Neighbors Association gives neighbors a place to hear about projects and respond.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: PAX Cafe, 2336 S. 18th Street, Philadelphia, PA

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the group's website, or email the listed contact, to ask where and when the group meets, since the site lists neither.
first_step.basis: The website is marked as a new site in development. It names no meetings, events or join steps, only a contact form, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit, and it lists no meetings, events or costs. The contact form asks for a name, an email and the reason you are writing. The meeting place is known only from the City list, so confirm it before you go.
first_visit_tips: Ask where and when the group meets, since the site does not say.
The group also has a Facebook page listed on the City list; confirm any dates posted there with the group.

records.notes: Shares its website (girardestateneighbors.org) with the GEAR record, and the site identifies itself as Girard Estate Neighbors Association, so the two records may be one group under two registered names. The reviewer should decide whether to merge them. The site's only date is a 2026 copyright footer, so status is probably_active and the City registry date is kept. The website was previously listed as a Facebook page; that page is now kept as a social link and was not read. Meeting place is from the City list and is not confirmed by the site.

records.name: Greater Philadelphia Community Alliance
records.summary: A South Philadelphia nonprofit that runs family programs, including early learning and free Pre-K, after-school and summer camps, benefits and bill help, and adult and parent classes. It also includes a Neighborhood Advisory Committee for the area.
records.what_you_do: Families use its early learning classes, after-school and summer camps, benefits and bill help, housing and utility help, and adult classes, including parenting and English as a second language classes. The site lists a Neighborhood Advisory Committee but does not say how to join it.

first_step.how: For free Pre-K, use the registration link on the group's preschool page (gpcacares.org/programs/preschool). For other programs, call (215) 336-5505 or email info@gpca-phila.org.
first_step.basis: Programs are described as free or low cost and open to Philadelphia residents of all ages, and the site gives a phone line and an email. Eligibility, hours and sign-up steps are not stated for most programs.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical visit. Programs serve young children, school-age kids, teens, parents and adults, and several are free or low cost. Hours, locations and sign-up steps are listed for only some programs, so call the office first.
first_visit_tips: Call the office with the name of the program you want before you go.
Ask about eligibility, cost and hours, since the site leaves most of these out.
Pick the center nearest you from the contact page, which gives the address for each one.

records.notes: Tier 1 described this group only as a Neighborhood Advisory Committee. The group's own site describes a family services nonprofit formed in 2022 from a merger of two earlier agencies, with the Neighborhood Advisory Committee as one part of its community development work, so kind, summary, categories and interests were changed. Eligibility for most programs is not stated. A book bag drive is listed with an August 5, 2026 date but its title says 2025, so it was not used. The site's general contact is info@gpca-phila.org and (215) 336-5505; the tier 1 contact email is kept. The Get Involved link is a placeholder. The Lincoln Education Center is listed as opening fall 2026 and is left out. Adult ESL classes are described in what_you_do but have no exact tag in the vocabulary.

records.name: Growing Homes Community Garden
records.summary: A community garden on Emily Street in South Philadelphia, organized by SEAMAAC with partners. It was set up to help newly arrived refugees and newcomers eat well, grow familiar crops and settle into the neighborhood.
records.what_you_do: Gardeners grow crops in the community garden with SEAMAAC and its partners, the Neighborhood Gardens Trust and the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society. The site does not describe workdays.

first_step.how: Email the garden's SEAMAAC contact address to ask how to get a plot and whether there is a waitlist.
first_step.basis: The garden was set up for newcomers and refugees, but the site gives no steps for getting a plot, no waitlist details and no eligibility rules. The only way in is an email address.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical visit or workday. It says the program works with about 150 gardeners, mostly immigrant and refugee, in an update that is not dated. Ask about plots and fees before you come, since the site does not list them.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether there is a plot waitlist before you visit.
Ask about fees, and whether tools and water are provided, since the site does not say.

records.notes: The SEAMAAC pages say the gardens were established in 2010 on the 700 block of Emily Street and the 500 block of Mercy Street, which fits 742 Emily St. The COVID-era update is undated and the 2021 footer is copyright, so status is probably_active and the tier 1 registry date is kept. The site does not say whether gardens are individual plots. The gardener email on the page is obfuscated, so the address comes from the City registry. Not verified on the site. SEAMAAC is the operator and is listed as a lead. Neighborhood Gardens Trust and Pennsylvania Horticultural Society are named as partners and are listed as leads.
